title: Consumption fingerprint rotation and compact reconciliation for retry-safe billing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: At-least-once request ingestion and network-level retries can cause observed consumption to be recorded multiple times or be left in an ambiguous state. Existing mitigation (opaque replay tokens) covers many cases but leaves gaps for long-lived streaming requests, multi-region failovers, and partial-response scenarios. This ticket proposes a compact, per-request fingerprint rotation scheme paired with a lightweight reconciliation sweep to provide idempotent consumption semantics while preserving low-latency edge acceptance.
design_goals: Guarantee single-charge semantics for a request id under common retry patterns without adding significant tail latency
Support streaming/long-running requests where token lifetimes need rotation
Remain compatible with multi-region routing and offline-edge scenarios
Minimize storage footprint in edge caches and central ledgers
Provide clear audit trail for reconciliations and disputes
proposal_summary: Assign clients an opaque client-id if not present and accept an optional "idempotency_token" per logical request

Create a short (64-bit) request fingerprint computed from (client-id | idempotency_token | truncated-hash-of-first-bytes) and a monotonically-incrementing ephemeral rotation counter maintained by the edge ingress
Edge writes a tentative consumption entry keyed by fingerprint+rotation into local fast-store (Redis/LMDB) with TTL slightly longer than expected retry window

On final commit (successful delivery or definitive failure), edge issues a confirmation record to central ledger. Central ledger deduplicates by fingerprint and rotation to decide final billing events
Periodic compact reconciliation job coalesces tentative entries older than X into final decisions using heuristics and request traces to reduce stale records
If client reconnects after rotation, the edge can present the previous fingerprint to central ledger to avoid double-charge when safe
tradeoffs_and_considerations: Rotation counter adds complexity for multi-edge ticket handoffs; we limit rotation footprints by bounding counter and preferring central checkpoint on long-lived sessions
Tentative entries mean billing is optimistic until confirm; to avoid visible customer charge volatility, we will only surface confirmed charges to billing UI until reconciliation completes
Choosing fingerprint length balances collision risk vs storage. 64-bit selected as pragmatic default with monitoring for collision rates
This is complementary to existing ack-token approaches; we will phase integration to avoid duplication in logic
edge_cases: Client-side resends with mutated idempotency_token — treated as new logical request
Cross-region failover where different edges generated different rotations — reconciliation will use request traces and timestamps to pick winner
Partial streaming where first N tokens delivered and rest retried — we record interim consumption and reconcile final total on commit
Ambiguous timeouts where client and server disagree on completion: mark tentative and escalate to reconciliation after grace window
acceptance_criteria: No increase in duplicate billing incidents for test workload with synthetic at-least-once retries (target <1 per 10M requests)
Edge RTT impact <2ms median for request acceptance path when fingerprinting enabled
Reconciliation job completes within configured window for 99% of tentative records
Audit logs contain fingerprint -> final ledger mapping for every reconciled request
implementation_steps: 1) Add idempotency_token header support in ingress proxy and client SDKs (opt-in) [ENG SDK PR link pending]
2) Implement fingerprint generator in edge acceptor and store tentative entries in Redis LMDB shim
3) Central ledger: accept confirmation RPCs keyed by fingerprint+rotation and deduplicate
4) Implement compact reconciliation worker with conservative heuristics and trace lookup capability
5) Add migration flag and feature gate in console to opt-in per-customer
6) Run canary on low-traffic tenants, expand to dedicated hosts, then global rollout
test_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint collisions and rotation handling
Integration tests simulating packet loss, delayed confirms, multi-region failover
Chaos tests: kill edge during commit to ensure reconciliation recovers without double-charge
Load tests to validate Redis TTL pressure and reconciliation throughput
Billing e2e test comparing baseline vs new scheme on synthetic retry-heavy workload
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: tentative_entries_growth_rate > threshold -> page on potential leak
Dashboard: per-customer tentative->confirmed ratio and disputed charge count
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (dev): SDK + edge support behind dev flag; run unit/integration tests
Stage 1 (canary): Enable for 5 internal tenants, monitor reconciliation and collision metrics
Stage 2 (beta): Open opt-in for customers via console flag; run billing comparisons and collect feedback
Stage 3 (gradual): Default-on for new tenants and recommended for existing after 2 weeks stabilization
Stage 4 (enforce): Consider making idempotency token required for high-throughput dedicated contracts in runtime-1.21
